sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement Deed/Memorandum of Understanding dated 01.06.2022.
Copy of the said settlement is placed on record.

Accordingly, the petition under Section 13-B(2) of the HMA Act was allowed and the marriage of the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was dissolved vide decree dated 03.02.2023 passed by the Principal Judge, Family Courts, North,
Rohini Courts, Delhi.

sentences.text: The copy of the decree is already on record.
6. Petitioner nos. 1 to 4 & 6 are present in Court today and petitioner no.5 is appearing through video-conferencing.
Respondent No.2 is also present in Court today and she has been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
As per settlement, today, a demand draft of Rs. 2,50,000/- (bearing no. 172599 dated 04.10.2023, drawn on Bank of Baroda) has been handed over to respondent no.2.
Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
7. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question be quashed.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/10/2023 at 02:23:37 8.
Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.1181/2021,
under Section 498A/406/377/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Bawana, Delhi, and the proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.
9.
The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J OCTOBER 19, 2023/akc
